\chapter{Cheap and Goods: No New Signs}
\label{ch:mw-shopping-five}
\hlchaptermodality{19}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can add cheap and goods to the shop-item-price map in listening, speaking, reading, and writing without learning another sign.}

Two more source-attested shopping words reuse the secure script inventory and join the earlier three in a non-compensatory four-skill payoff.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[sastā]{Hear \emph{sastā} — cheap}

\label{lesson:MW-C14-hear-sasta}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-word shopping payoff, say price, write \textbf{\mw{ु}}, \textbf{\mw{दुकान}}, \textbf{\mw{वस्तु}}, \textbf{\mw{भाव}}, and \textbf{\mw{भाई}}, then say heat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{sastā} — \textbf{cheap; inexpensive}
\end{quote}

Say the two beats once from a low-price cue. This is the source's dictionary form; full bargaining phrases remain later work.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sastā]{\mw{सस्ता} — cheap on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C14-sasta}



\begin{quote}
Say cheap and price. Write \textbf{\mw{भाव}}, \textbf{\mw{वस्तु}}, \textbf{\mw{बरसात}}, and \textbf{\mw{पति}}, say sister, then recall \textbf{\mw{्}} and \textbf{\mw{त}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{सस्}} + \textbf{\mw{ता}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{सस्ता}} — \emph{sastā} — cheap
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{सस्ता}}. Check the middle consonant join and final long \textbf{\mw{ा}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sāmān]{Hear \emph{sāmān} — goods}

\label{lesson:MW-C14-hear-samaan}



\begin{quote}
Say and write cheap and shop, recall item and price, then write home, sister, and \textbf{\mw{गर्मी}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{sāmān} — \textbf{goods; merchandise}
\end{quote}

Hear the two long-vowel beats and say the word once from a group-of-items cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sāmān]{\mw{सामान} — goods on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C14-samaan}



\begin{quote}
Say goods and cheap. Write \textbf{\mw{सस्ता}}, \textbf{\mw{दुकान}}, \textbf{\mw{वस्तु}}, \textbf{\mw{मौसम}}, and \textbf{\mw{नाम}}, retrieve the four-word family payoff, then form \textbf{\mw{ा}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{सा}} + \textbf{\mw{मान}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{सामान}} — \emph{sāmān} — goods
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{सामान}}. Check both long \textbf{\mw{ा}} marks and the final \textbf{\mw{न}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve cheap and goods}

\label{lesson:MW-R14-shopping-new-two}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-word shopping payoff, then write \textbf{\mw{ु}}, \textbf{\mw{ौ}}, \textbf{\mw{ग}}, and \textbf{\mw{ड}}, then say paternal grandfather and cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the two words in both orders, give each meaning, read two cards, then write both from sound.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}; \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — five shopping words in four skills}

\label{lesson:MW-C14-shopping-five}



\begin{quote}
Recall the earlier shopping and weather payoffs, say money, then write \textbf{\mw{द}} and \textbf{\mw{ड}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. Identify five heard words. 2. Produce five words from meaning cues. 3. Match five printed cards to meanings. 4. Write all five heard words without a model.

Pass each skill separately; a strong word cannot compensate for a missed one.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the five-word shopping loop}

\label{lesson:MW-R14-shopping-close}



\begin{quote}
Write short \textbf{\mw{ु}}, then ask and answer the known name and wellbeing exchanges, then write \textbf{\mw{दादा}} and \textbf{\mw{ठंडी}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Without a model, hear two words, say two from meaning cues, read the fifth, then write all five in a fresh mixed order.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Sources: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}; \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
